To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce an encoder-decoder pipeline that unifies image text embedding and language models, 2) we introduce a novel language model, the Structure Content neural language model, that disentangles structure and content in a sentence, and 3) we set new state of the art results on Flickr30K and 8K without using object detection.

1) we introduce a novel language model that learns to generate novel descriptions from a learned joint embedding space, 2) the language model is conditioned on the structure of a given sentence and the content of a given image, 3) we show that our language model is capable of learning to describe images without using object detections, and 4) we show that the learned embedding space is capable of representing multimodal regularities.
we introduce an encoder-decoder pipeline that unifies joint embedding models with multimodality language models and achieves state of the art results in the Flickr8K and Flicker30K datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of unifying multimodal learning and neural machine translation.
the problem of learning multimodal representations that are both semantically and visually grounded, while also being able to produce natural language descriptions of images from scratch.
learning a joint embedding space that captures the semantic content of images and text, while allowing us to generate novel text from the space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work unifies the best of both worlds: multimodal joint embedding models with neural language models.
the proposed method is a novel and effective way to learn a joint embedding space with image and text, and a language model for decoding representations in this space.
we have developed a new multimodal neural language model for describing images that unifies joint image sentence embedding models with language modeling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we learn an image text space that is both good for ranking and generation.
we have developed a unified multimodal embedding and language model that learns to rank images and generate captions from scratch.
we have introduced a new model that unifies multimodal embedding models with multimodality aware language models, which can be trained with a single loss function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model can be used as an alternative to the current state of the art image and video captioning systems.
the structure content neural model is able to learn to generate novel captions for images and sentences.
multimodal language models have the potential to learn joint embeddings for image text pairs.
